target.title: fix(config): preserve recovery state during config-health migration
target.body:
Closes #99280

Related: #99327, #99364

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading from the legacy config-health JSON store to shared SQLite could receive a permanent migration warning on routine CLI commands. In the affected upgrade order, SQLite could observe a newer valid config before migration while still lacking the legacy promoted recovery fingerprint; the whole-row comparison then treated the two useful states as conflicting, retained the legacy source, and left last-known-good recovery unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The migration now reconciles fields according to their ownership instead of comparing entire serialized rows. Existing non-null SQLite fingerprints remain authoritative, missing known/promoted fingerprints are filled from legacy state, absent paths are imported, and SQLite suspicious-signature state is preserved. The legacy source is retired only after the transaction succeeds; a source regenerated by a released macOS writer is removed without overwriting its existing archive.

This keeps one canonical SQLite runtime path while preserving the recovery state that the legacy store uniquely owns during upgrade.

## User Impact

Affected upgrades no longer emit the permanent config-health conflict warning. Their existing `.last-good` backup remains eligible for automatic recovery, newer valid SQLite observations are not rolled back, and old app builds cannot recreate the warning loop after migration.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts -- --reporter=dot`
  - 42 tests passed on the current branch head.
- `pnpm check:changed`
  - Passed core production/test typechecks, lint, database-first guards, and import-cycle checks on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwn6e54584mmgjt72w07pwp4`.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`
  - Clean; no accepted or actionable findings.
- Live AWS Crabbox upgrade comparison, run `run_dc83fd068afe`, lease `cbx_1b643cfb42ff`:
  - Published `openclaw@2026.6.9` created the legacy JSON and `.last-good` baseline.
  - `origin/main` reproduced `warning=present recovery=false`.
  - The candidate produced `warning=absent recovery=true regenerated_source=retired`.
  - The candidate proof used pre-rebase commit `0f1bb4e591`; the two touched files are byte-identical at current head `e16356353f`.

AI-assisted implementation. I reviewed the migration ownership, transaction behavior, tests, and live proof.
